veranderings.voor: Dit kan 'n plek, gebou of voorwerp wees.
veranderings.na: Dit kan 'n plek, 'n gebou of 'n voorwerp wees.
veranderings.rede: Repeating the article before each item reads more naturally and makes the three separate things clearer for Grade 5.

veranderings.voor: UNESCO erken plekke van waarde vir die hele mensdom as wêrelderfenisterreine.
veranderings.na: UNESCO erken plekke wat vir die hele mensdom waardevol is, as wêrelderfenisterreine.
veranderings.rede: 'Plekke van waarde vir' is stiff and nominal; a relative clause is more natural, echoes the glossary wording, and the comma stops 'waardevol is as' being misread.
Small numbers in running prose usually read better written out in words; the number itself is unchanged.

veranderings.voor: Robbeneiland is ook kultureel omdat dit ons laat dink aan belangrike mense en wat daar gebeur het.
veranderings.na: Robbeneiland is ook kultureel, want dit laat ons dink aan belangrike mense en aan wat daar gebeur het.
veranderings.rede: Matches the 'X is ..., want ...' pattern of the neighbouring sentences, fixes the subordinate-clause word order ('dit ons laat dink aan'), and repeats 'aan' so both objects attach clearly to 'dink'.
The compound 'goudplaatjies' is the natural Afrikaans form; 'plaatjies goud' reads like a translation.

vlae.teks: Musiek, feeste en jou gesin se stories is nie-tasbaar. Jy kan dit nie vashou nie.
vlae.rede: The study text defines tangible with 'sien en aanraak' and the glossary defines intangible with 'nie kan aanraak nie', but this sentence uses 'vashou'. Not a language fault and not changed, because aligning the verb may touch a shared definition pair; noting it in case the writer wants the study text to use the same verb as the glossary.
